name: Notification Triggers (abandoned)
plain: Scheduled local notifications that fire without a server; not shipped.
meaning: Would have let a site schedule notifications for a future time without push. Chrome ran an origin trial and then dropped it, so no browser ships it.

access.prompt_ui: Needed notification permission plus an origin trial token.

limits.headline: Can't schedule a notification for later without a server; no browser ships it
limits.user_action: Nothing. Chrome tried an experiment, then dropped it
can: Show a normal notification when a server sends one, which is a different feature
Use a reminder style app that depends on push instead
cannot: Schedule a future notification from the page alone
Skip the notification permission, which it would still have needed

story.what_it_is: A plan to let sites schedule alerts that fire without a server. It was dropped and not released.
story.for_you: You will not see this feature. It was tested but never shipped. Scheduled alerts still need a server push or your app to be open.
story.for_makers: Makers wanted to set reminders on the device without paying for a push server. Browser makers stopped the work. Developers use push messages or local checks instead.

use_cases.example: A calendar web app wanted to schedule a reminder for a meeting an hour from now, with no server.
A medicine reminder site wanted daily alerts on the device, even when offline.
A farming browser game wanted a ping when crops finish growing, with no push server.
A travel app wanted a boarding reminder two hours before a flight without a connection.
A language app wanted a daily practice nudge that works offline.
A workout site wanted timers that alert you after rest periods while the tab sleeps.
A store wanted to remind shoppers of a sale start time without a server.

technical_bounds: Replaced by calendar apps and push

history.change: Trial ended and the feature was abandoned
